{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABbIPaAQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhEtYFQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 164, "title": "Add a Speaker output Node for automatic sequential live TTS playback", "body": "## Problem

The existing `AudioOutput` ("Audio player / WAV") creates a separate manually operated player and download link for **every** `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO` result. That is useful for listening to or exporting an individual clip, but it does not meet the live TTS use case: audio should go to the system's **default speaker** as soon as each result is ready, with no Play click per clip.

## Expected outcome

Add a separate, minimal output Node for continuous speaker playback while **retaining the existing manual Audio player / WAV Node unchanged**.

```text
ASR.final / Translator.text  →  Supertonic3.text (or Kokoro.text)
TTS.audio: SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO →  SpeakerOutput.audio: SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO
```

- Name the node clearly in the Graph Editor, e.g. **Speaker** / `SpeakerOutput`; put it in the existing **Outputs** category.
- The Node accepts only `audio: SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO`, with no output ports. When synthesized audio arrives, it is **automatically played through the browser's default audio output**. No per-clip player, WAV download, extra settings, or device picker in this Node.
- **Serialize playback**: if a clip is currently playing, enqueue the next clip and play it immediately after the previous one ends. Keep arrival order, avoid overlaps and unintended replay/duplication. This is successive playback of completed TTS clips, not a claim of sample-by-sample streaming or zero latency.
- Keep the implementation local and simple. Reuse existing audio validation/conversion if helpful; do not add an external playback service or new model manager.
- Handle browser autoplay/user-activation constraints correctly: initialize/unlock audio from the existing explicit **Start** user gesture where allowed, and show a concise actionable way to enable playback if the browser blocks it; never silently swallow the failure.
- Bound the playback queue or apply suitable backpressure. If output is generated faster than it can be played, report overflow explicitly rather than accumulating unlimited audio or silently dropping clips.
- Keep lifecycle predictable: Start resets playback state; Stop drains already accepted generated audio and queued playback in order (or documents an existing stop-compatible limitation without losing audio silently); Cancel immediately halts output and clears the queue; close/dispose stops playback and releases resources. No late replies from a previous session should start playing.
- Output only from the session's extension UI; make the requirement to keep the live window open explicit if that is how the architecture works. Do not make background playback claims unless actually supported.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graph Editor offers a clearly named Speaker output Node, connectable via `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO` from both existing TTS Nodes; Save/reload and graph validation work.
- [ ] Two or more generated clips start without individual Play clicks, play in arrival order, never overlap, and do not restart older clips on later emissions.
- [ ] Browser default speaker works for a Start-triggered live session; autoplay restrictions and missing audio output fail with clear user feedback and a usable recovery action.
- [ ] Stop, Cancel, repeated Start, queue saturation and window close behave predictably and release audio/audio URLs; no runaway memory or silent lost audio.
- [ ] Existing `Audio player / WAV` remains available with its current manual playback/download behavior; old saved graphs are unchanged and need no migration solely because a new Node type is added.
- [ ] Focused unit, browser and packaged MV3 tests cover consecutive TTS clips and lifecycle, using controlled audio fixtures; document any model/hardware dependent validation that cannot run.
- [ ] No new navigation mode, persistent playback toolbar, output device picker, framework or speculative audio abstraction.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

- `extension/graph.js`: `Supertonic3`, `Kokoro`, `AudioOutput` definitions.
- `extension/graph-runtime.js`: current sink and `onSynthesizedAudio` callback.
- `extension/recorder.js`: existing per-clip HTML audio player and WAV download behavior.
- `web/tts-nodes.js`, `web/synthesized-audio.js`, `docs/extension-graph.md`.
- Keep user-facing UI minimal: **Keep it simple / Show, don't tell / Intuitive and predictable**.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/164", "created_at": "2026-10-30T08:08:34Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/my-audio-to-text", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "a5ffc7c822d94a90b967ad623f093538"}
